title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Outdoor Education and Safety
subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following precautions is most important in preventing blisters while hiking?
options: keeping cool on hot days to prevent feet from sweating
wearing two pairs of socks so no air circulates next to skin
remaining hydrated and warming up before hikes on cold days
wearing sturdy, proper-fitting hiking shoes that have been broken in
questions.explain: Blisters are caused by friction and pressure. The most important preventative measure is wearing well-fitting, broken-in footwear that does not rub against the skin. Ill-fitting shoes are the primary cause of blisters on hikes.

questions.q: Bicyclists can best ensure that they are visible to motorists during daylight hours by:
options: wearing bright or fluorescent-colored clothing.
attaching a battery-operated headlight to their bicycles.
wearing a white or light-colored helmet or jacket.
attaching a small flag to the rear of their bicycles.
questions.explain: During daylight hours, bright and fluorescent colors are the most eye-catching and provide the greatest contrast against most backgrounds, making a bicyclist more visible to motorists than plain white clothing or small accessories.

questions.q: In an outdoor education curriculum, which of the following practices is most likely to help students develop an ethic of stewardship toward the natural environment?
options: instructing students how to pack as lightly as possible for hikes and camping trips
familiarizing students with the locations of national parks, wildlife refuges, and forests in their region
teaching students Leave No Trace principles and how to apply them in any outdoor setting
arranging to have students participate in annual National Public Lands Day activities
questions.explain: The Leave No Trace principles are a specific, widely adopted ethical framework designed to teach people how to interact with the environment responsibly. Learning and applying these principles directly fosters an ethic of environmental stewardship.

questions.q: Which of the following techniques should be used by a belayer to ensure the safety of a climber during indoor rock climbing?
options: signaling to the climber each time the climber should move up the wall
maintaining some slack in the climbing rope at all times
keeping the brake hand in the "lock off" position when there is no slack or movement by the climber
maintaining a secure position beneath the climber and as close to the wall as possible
questions.explain: A belayer's primary job is to manage the rope to catch a fall. When not actively taking in or paying out rope, the brake hand must securely hold the rope in the 'lock off' position to ensure an immediate brake if the climber falls. Too much slack (B) is dangerous.

questions.q: Involving students in outdoor education courses such as orienteering, canoeing, hiking, and rock climbing is particularly effective for promoting students' self-esteem, because the activities include built-in opportunities to:
options: block out distractions completely and become meditative.
experience a sense of accomplishment in reaching a goal or destination.
enjoy time on one's own and focus on the body mechanics of the activity.
attempt to set personal best records each time one participates.
questions.explain: These activities involve working toward a clear, tangible goal (e.g., reaching a summit, navigating to a point). Achieving these goals provides a powerful and immediate sense of accomplishment, which in turn builds self-confidence and self-esteem.
